objections.objection: 'Bun main thread Atomics.wait while a worker runs the kipc CALL' is stated as a mechanism without its identity atom. The live Bun client is a single `Bun.connect` socket with async handlers owned by the main thread; a Worker cannot share that socket, so the worker needs its OWN app-link connection with its own HELLO and possession secret. Whether the host admits a second authenticated link for the same principal generation (a 'sync sidecar link') is an unowned permission-model/wire decision, not a facade detail. Until that is specified, the Atomics.wait probe proves only that the main thread can park, not that a sync dialog can be emulated. And this is on draw.io's primary_workflow: `dialog.showMessageBoxSync` runs inside the `isModified-result` handler on every close of a dirty document.

(b) is a second authenticated link = a second principal minted for the same role and is refused outright (identity is link metadata, 02 §1/KEL-97). (a) is a client redesign whose ordering and backpressure semantics must be specified (KEL-80 owner) before the spike, otherwise the spike measures a prototype that cannot ship.

objections.question: q1/q4
objections.objection: The claim that a blocking main-process CALL is cheap because 'Bun's client is already a blocking reader (echo_call)' is false for the shipping link, and the proposed showMessageBoxSync-as-blocking-kipc-CALL would deadlock as designed. The one FrameReader the facade is allowed to have runs on the Bun main-thread event loop (Bun.connect `data` callbacks); KEL-142 §4.2 forbids a second socket or overlapping readers. If the main thread parks (Atomics.wait or any synchronous wait) the REPLY it is waiting for can never be read. `echo_call` is a one-shot helper, not the persistent session loop. A blocking main-process CALL therefore requires relocating the single link into a Worker (every frame hops worker→main, allocation per frame on the hot path) — a design atom with measurable cost, not something already sanctioned by 02 §5.

objections.question: q4
objections.objection: 'Host suspends inbound-CALL deadlines while a role is parked in a modal CALL' invents a cross-call coupling rule for a deadline that does not exist at the layer named. 02 §7's deadline is a frame-stall clock (first byte of a frame to its last byte; idle polls retry), not a reply-wait deadline; KEL-142 defines no handler/reply deadline for a pending host CALL. The rule would make one modal CALL silently alter the contract of every other in-flight CALL (hidden coupling, atomic protocol rule 3) inside keld-ipc, which must stay free of Electron-isms. The root-cause design needs no suspension: make the close request a host EVENT `WindowCloseRequested(w, gen, req)` with the window parked in `close_pending` by the registry, and the facade's decision a Bun→host CALL `window.closeDecision(req, allow|veto)` — the direction the live v0 lifecycle already uses (host sends Event frames, Bun sends Call frames). The host never waits on Bun, nothing times out, and a second dirty window simply stays parked until its decision arrives.
